reasons.specificity: The inventory closely tracks the article’s distinctive pillars, competing AUKUS interpretations, actor fractions, regulatory mechanisms, and militarised-neoliberal framework.
reasons.anchoring: Most quotations occur in the source and support the classifications, though some inferred labels—especially governments treating Pillar I as a deliverable sovereign capability—exceed the quoted wording.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes actor type from policy mechanism, identifies critical-mineral firms as boundary cases, and exposes conditional bipartisanship and the structural role assigned to venture capital.
reasons.coherence: The four-dimensional scheme is largely consistent, but government-owned British Technology Investments is grouped with financial/venture capital and several bilateral projects oscillate between formal Pillar II instances and merely adjacent activity.
reasons.usefulness: The extensive inventory and contested-case ledger are valuable with the text open, but the requested boundary-and-overlap table is not actually supplied and context-dependent membership criteria remain scattered across sections.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Claims generally reproduce or cautiously reconstruct the article, but some counts are arbitrary, several cited secondary works are treated as independently supporting categories, and formal AUKUS status is occasionally inferred from a wider defence environment.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: K5 attributes to the Australian, US, and UK governments the classification of Pillar I as a “Deliverable sovereign capability,” reasoning that submarine transfer “will produce an Australian capability.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The source says only that the US and UK “reinforced their support for Australia’s acquisition” through infrastructure, technical capabilities, and human capital, while separately warning that delays and congressional resistance could leave Australia “with no sovereign submarine capability.”

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: The response presents cross-classifications and scattered boundary labels as fulfillment of the requested boundary-and-overlap table.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: No consolidated table shows nonexclusive membership, disputed cases, and criteria that change by context; the source itself supplies context-sensitive distinctions such as relative US bipartisanship, internal Australian dissent, and bilateral projects whose formal Pillar II status is uncertain.

score.one_line: A highly source-specific and analytically strong inventory, weakened by omission of the requested boundary/overlap table and a few inferred statuses presented more firmly than the article supports.
